title: Black Hole Sound: How NASA Scaled It 57 Octaves Up
description:
Hear the real black hole sound captured by NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory inside the Perseus galaxy cluster—a haunting B-flat 57 octaves below middle C!

Roughly 250 million light-years from Earth, the Perseus galaxy cluster (centered on giant active galaxy NGC 1275) is wrapped in superheated 10-million-degree X-ray plasma spanning hundreds of thousands of light-years. While empty space is a silent vacuum, astronomers led by Prof. Andrew Fabian at the University of Cambridge analyzed 53 hours of NASA Chandra X-ray observations in 2003 and discovered concentric pressure ripples ~30,000 light-years wide rolling outward through that cluster gas.

Those ripples are true acoustic sound waves driven by relativistic black hole jets inflating giant cavities—oscillating once every ~10 million years (about 144 quadrillion times deeper than human ears can detect). In 2022, NASA extracted Chandra's radial X-ray waves and scaled them up 57 to 58 octaves into human hearing, revealing how black hole sound waves heat intracluster gas for billions of years so trillions of stars cannot chaotically collapse.
